patch.value: Agent distribution funnel: MCP Registry record, canonical portable Agent Skills, pm setup-agent, pm agent doctor, agent project profile, version-coherent plugins

Marketing to agents is product distribution: agents discover and select tools through registry records, tool/skill metadata, repo guidance, trust metadata, and context cost — not blog posts. Build the machine-facing acquisition funnel on existing assets (pm-mcp binary, Claude/Codex skills, profile system, health/doctor infrastructure).

pm-mcp published to the official MCP Registry with verified namespace, version-pinned launch command, transports, runtime requirement, permissions/local-data behavior; one canonical portable Agent Skills source tree derives the Claude and Codex skill packages (no hand-maintained copies) with trigger-oriented descriptions plus positive and near-miss trigger tests; pm setup-agent <client|all> detects the client, installs/updates skills, configures version-pinned MCP, selects a tool profile, verifies handshake, and runs a read-only pm context smoke test; pm agent doctor verifies runtime, workspace discovery, MCP launch, profile, skill/plugin versions, contract compatibility, context read, token size, and mutation identity; an agent project profile (pm profile apply agent) composes pm-brief, pm-context, compact context depth, search defaults, and minimal guidance; generated repository guidance stays tiny (a few pm commands + contracts pointer, detail lives in skills/pm guide); Codex plugin never silently runs a newer @latest MCP server than the installed plugin (bundle, pin, or fail clearly — same class as pm-l9wl on the Claude side)

# Agent distribution funnel

Humans discover via posts/demos/search. Agents discover and select via: tool names+descriptions, skill metadata, repository instructions, MCP registry records, resources/prompts, trust+permission metadata, context cost, and successful prior calls. Funnel stages:

    DISCOVERY  registry, package metadata, agent skill, AGENTS.md, plugin marketplace
    SELECTION  tool description quality, trigger accuracy, small active surface, trust metadata
    ACTIVATION workspace detection, init, health/doctor, first context result
    VALUE      correct next work, successful claim, useful handoff, evidence-backed close
    RETENTION  session hook, durable history, new-session continuity, low context cost

## Canonical Agent Skills package (derive Claude + Codex from ONE source tree, portable SKILL.md format)
Recommended skills and triggers: pm-orient (starting/resuming work in a pm repository) · pm-triage (turning a request into duplicate-checked structured work) · pm-plan (creating/updating a durable implementation plan) · pm-deliver (claim, implement, link evidence, validate, close) · pm-handoff (compact context for another agent/session) · pm-review (health, duplicates, missing metadata, project integrity checks) · pm-package-author (building/testing a pm SDK package). Each skill: precise trigger-oriented description (optimized for triggering, not marketing prose), explicit use-when / do-not-use-when boundaries, short core procedure, on-demand references, positive trigger tests, near-miss negative tests, output-quality evals. Example description: "Use when starting, resuming, triaging, planning, implementing, verifying, or handing off repository work managed under .agents/pm. Prefer pm context, pm next, and search before creating or mutating items."

## MCP Registry (preview — keep editor-specific setup paths too)
Canonical record: stable package identifier, version-pinned launch command, supported transports, runtime requirement, tool profiles, permissions + local-data behavior, repo/docs metadata, checksums/provenance where supported. Verify the namespace.

## MCP resources and prompts (reduce pressure to make every behavior a tool)
Resources: pm://workspace/context, pm://workspace/contracts, pm://workspace/schema, pm://workflow/orient, pm://workflow/deliver, pm://workflow/handoff, pm://packages/catalog. Prompts: pm-start-work, pm-triage-request, pm-create-plan, pm-close-with-evidence, pm-handoff.

## pm setup-agent (build on existing pm init --agent-guidance, do not replace it)
    pm setup-agent claude|codex|cursor|vscode|gemini|windsurf|all
1 detect client, 2 install/update canonical skills, 3 configure MCP with version-pinned runtime, 4 add minimal repo guidance, 5 select default tool profile, 6 verify handshake + tool list, 7 read-only pm context smoke test, 8 print exact next steps.

## pm agent doctor (support tool AND onboarding conversion tool)
    pm agent doctor [--client claude|codex] [--json]
Checks: runtime version, workspace discovery, MCP launch, tool profile, skill install+version, plugin/runtime compatibility, package activation, contract compatibility, context read, token size, mutation identity, optional search-provider health. Builds on existing health/validate/package-doctor infrastructure.

## agent project profile (use the existing profile system — profiles already compose schema, workflows, config, templates, recommended packages)
`pm profile apply agent`: recommends pm-brief + pm-context + guide-shell + linked-test adapters, agent-oriented workflow defaults, compact context depth, search defaults, minimal guidance. Advanced semantic search stays optional.

## Tiny repository guidance (generated; giant AGENTS.md files are an anti-goal — fence note (4) on pm-wjfa)
    ## Project context
    This repository uses pm.
    - Start with pm context --limit 10 or pm next.
    - Search before creating work. Claim before mutating.
    - Link relevant files, docs, and tests. Close with evidence and a reason.
    - pm contracts --summary --json for the active machine surface.

## Version coherence
The Codex plugin must not silently run a newer @latest MCP server than the installed plugin: bundle the matching runtime, pin the npm version in generated launcher metadata, resolve the plugin version and request exactly it, or fail clearly. Claude-side marketplace @latest fallback is owned by pm-l9wl (related) — fix per-plugin, same class. Version coherence is part of the trust story.

value.text: Skill-duplication measurement (ecosystem review 2026-07-25) for the 'one canonical portable Agent Skills source tree' half of this item's AC. Twelve SKILL.md files live under three unrelated roots: .agents/skills (pm-developer, pm-user, pm-extensions, pm-sdk), plugins/pm-claude/skills (pm-workflow, pm-audit, pm-planner, pm-developer, pm-release), plugins/pm-codex/skills (pm-native, pm-auditor, pm-release). Two names are maintained twice over — pm-developer exists in .agents/skills (74 lines, bash/CLI phrasing) and plugins/pm-claude/skills (116 lines, MCP tool phrasing); pm-release exists in both plugin trees and diverges by 90 diff lines, with the Claude copy carrying a Hybrid TUI Sync section the Codex copy lacks and the Codex copy carrying compatibility-gate steps the Claude copy lacks. The same is true of the audit pair (pm-audit vs pm-auditor). scripts/release/docs-skills-gate.mjs only asserts existence of the four .agents/skills entries plus frontmatter validity; nothing compares the harness copies, so the release loop can drift per harness indefinitely. No new item filed: this is evidence for the existing AC clause.

value.author: harness:claude-code
value.text:
Skill-root divergence census 2026-07-25 (evening ecosystem review), measured by content hash rather than name, sharpening the earlier "duplication across 3 roots" observation this item's AC already covers.

Three tracked skill roots hold 12 SKILL.md files:
- .agents/skills — pm-developer, pm-extensions, pm-sdk, pm-user (plus HARNESS_COMPATIBILITY.md and README.md)
- plugins/pm-claude/skills — pm-audit, pm-developer, pm-planner, pm-release, pm-workflow
- plugins/pm-codex/skills — pm-auditor, pm-native, pm-release

The finding is that the overlapping names are NOT copies, they have DIVERGED, which is worse than duplication because each root silently teaches an agent something different:
- pm-developer exists in .agents/skills (74 lines) and plugins/pm-claude/skills (123 lines) with different content hashes.
- pm-release exists in plugins/pm-claude/skills (82 lines) and plugins/pm-codex/skills (19 lines) with different content hashes — a 4x size gap for the same nominal skill, so a Codex-harness agent and a Claude-harness agent given "the pm release skill" receive materially different instructions.
- pm-audit (claude) and pm-auditor (codex) are near-synonym names for the same role, which defeats name-based dedupe entirely and is also a naming-policy problem given the standing rule against the word "audit" in this project's own tracker vocabulary.

Consequence for this item's "one canonical skill source" AC: the fix cannot be a straight de-duplication pass, because there is no single surviving version to keep. It needs a canonical source plus a per-harness projection (or explicit, reviewed per-harness overrides), and a gate that fails when two roots ship the same skill name with different content. Without the gate the roots re-diverge on the next edit to any one of them.

value.text:
Skill-corpus drift measured 2026-07-26, extending the 'duplication across 3 roots' observation already routed here — the roots have now diverged, so this is no longer only a duplication problem.

Twelve SKILL.md files across three roots:

  plugins/pm-claude/skills/  pm-planner 147, pm-workflow 144, pm-developer 123, pm-audit 84, pm-release 82
  plugins/pm-codex/skills/   pm-native 69, pm-auditor 20, pm-release 19
  .agents/skills/            pm-developer 74, pm-user 60, pm-extensions 58, pm-sdk 51

Same-named skills, different content. pm-developer exists at two roots at 123 and 74 lines with 184 diff lines between them — the two copies share almost nothing verbatim, including the description line, which is the field a harness routes on. pm-release exists in both plugin roots at 82 and 19 lines, 89 diff lines. pm-audit and pm-auditor are the same skill under two names for two harnesses.

The drift is invisible to the gate. scripts/release/docs-skills-gate.mjs enforces per-file structure — frontmatter present, name matching the directory, a 'Use when' clause in the description, under 500 lines, guide routing markers, relative links resolvable, exactly one H1, and no duplicate section heading within a single file. Every one of those is a within-file check. There is no cross-file comparison of any kind, so two same-named skills can say opposite things and the gate stays green. The one duplication check that exists (line 437) fires only on a heading repeated inside one file.

Consequence for this item's canonical-source AC: the divergence means consolidation is now a merge with judgment calls rather than a deduplication, and the longer it runs the more expensive it gets. A cheap interim control worth having regardless of when consolidation lands: fail the gate when two SKILL.md files share a name across roots and their bodies differ beyond a declared allowance, so drift is at least announced.
